notes: Breadboard bank naming follows the catalogue (t = rows a-e, b = rows f-j); the picture labels the rows the other way round, so the top/bottom bank choice is a consistent mapping, not an exact row match.

Each LED's anode shares a column with its resistor (top bank); the cathode is one column to the right and is wired by a short black jumper to the top negative (GND) rail. Resistor lower leg and blue signal wire share a column in the other bank.
Blue wires go to Uno pins 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 (left to right) per the picture; schematic and code use pins 2-6 for the five LEDs.
The GND wire goes from the Uno GND pin beside AREF (GND.1) to the top negative rail (tn); exact rail hole numbers are approximate.
The Uno connects to the computer by USB for serial input; the USB cable is not drawn in the circuit image so it is not included.
Resistors are 220 ohm per the manual and schematic.
